question: What has each of the five actually disclosed about advisor compensation structures?
reasoning_content:

Let me review the passages. The key passages about advisor compensation structure:

EDJ-10K-2025#30: "Financial advisors are generally compensated on a commission basis, subject to a minimum guaranteed salary, and may be entitled to additional compensation based on their respective branch office profitability and the profitability of the Partnership."

EDJ-ADV-2026#64: "Most financial advisors receive a portion of the Program Fee, though some financial advisors receive a salary in addition to, or in lieu of, the Program Fee... The portion of the Program Fee paid to your financial advisor is at the discretion of Edward Jones."

EDJ-ADV-2026#67: mentions bonus, profits interest, travel award program.

EDJ-10K-2025#264 (from another sub-question): "Financial advisor bonuses are determined by the overall Partnership's profitability, as well as the performance of the individual financial advisors."

EDJ-10K-2025#221: non-qualified deferred compensation plan.

EDJ-10K-2025#222: retirement transition plans.

These are all facts about the advisor compensation structure.

Let me compile the facts:

1. EDJ-10K-2025#30 - commission basis, minimum guaranteed salary, additional compensation based on branch office profitability and Partnership profitability.

2. EDJ-ADV-2026#64 - most advisors receive a portion of Program Fee, some receive salary in addition or in lieu; portion of Program Fee paid is at discretion of Edward Jones; same fee rate regardless of model/program.

3. EDJ-ADV-2026#67 - Program Fee, assets under care, Reserve Line Advance balances impact bonus eligibility; eligibility for limited partnership profits interest; Travel Award Program based on new/existing assets under care.

4. EDJ-10K-2025#264 - financial advisor bonuses determined by overall Partnership profitability and performance of individual advisors.

5. EDJ-10K-2025#221 - non-qualified deferred compensation plan for certain financial advisors.

6. EDJ-10K-2025#222 - retirement transition plans for eligible retiring financial advisors.

7. EDJ-10K-2025#58 - bonuses paid to financial advisors may be decreased/eliminated if profitability decreases.

8. EDJ-10K-2025#31 - pay equity measures.

Let me focus on the compensation structure facts. The question is "what each firm has disclosed about its advisor compensation structure." This is broad, so I should include all relevant facts about the structure.

Let me select the key items:

Item 1 (from #30): Financial advisors compensated on commission basis, subject to minimum guaranteed salary, may receive additional compensation based on branch office profitability and Partnership profitability.

Item 2 (from #64): Most advisors receive a portion of Program Fee; some receive salary in addition to/in lieu of; portion paid at discretion of Edward Jones; fee rate same regardless of model/program.

Item 3 (from #67): Program Fee, assets under care, Reserve Line Advance balances impact bonus eligibility; eligibility for limited partnership profits interest; Travel Award Program based on new/existing assets under care.

Item 4 (from #264): Financial advisor bonuses determined by overall Partnership profitability and individual advisor performance.

Item 5 (from #221): Non-qualified deferred compensation plan for certain financial advisors.

Item 6 (from #222): Retirement transition plans.

cells.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones discloses that financial advisors are generally compensated on a commission basis, subject to a minimum guaranteed salary, and may be entitled to additional compensation based on their respective branch office profitability and the profitability of the Partnership.
items.quote: Financial advisors are generally compensated on a commission basis, subject to a minimum guaranteed salary, and may be entitled to additional compensation based on their respective branch office profitability and the profitability of the Partnership.

items.text: Edward Jones discloses that most financial advisors receive a portion of the Program Fee (though some receive a salary in addition to, or in lieu of, the Program Fee), that the portion of the Program Fee paid to a financial advisor is at the discretion of Edward Jones, and that the fee rate paid is the same regardless of the model or investment advisory program in which a client invests.
items.quote: Most financial advisors receive a portion of the Program Fee, though some financial advisors receive a salary in addition to, or in lieu of, the Program Fee. ... The portion of the Program Fee paid to your financial advisor is at the discretion of Edward Jones. The fee rate paid to your financial advisor will be the same regardless of the model in which you invest.

items.text: Edward Jones discloses that the Program Fee, assets under care and Reserve Line Advance balances impact most financial advisors' eligibility for a bonus and bonus amount, that these may also impact eligibility for certain limited partnership profits interest, and that most advisors are eligible for the Travel Award Program (domestic and international travel or a cash award) based on new and existing assets under care.
items.quote: The Program Fee, as well as assets under care and Reserve Line Advance balances, will impact most financial advisors' eligibility for a bonus and bonus amount. ... Most financial advisors are eligible to participate in the Edward Jones Travel Award Program ... Eligibility for the Travel Award Program is based upon the amount of new and existing assets under care of a financial advisor

items.text: Edward Jones discloses that financial advisor bonuses are determined by the overall Partnership's profitability, as well as the performance of the individual financial advisors.
items.quote: Financial advisor bonuses are determined by the overall Partnership's profitability, as well as the performance of the individual financial advisors.

items.text: Edward Jones discloses that the Partnership has a non-qualified deferred compensation plan for certain financial advisors, with a recorded liability of $303 for future payments due to financial advisors participating in the plan.
items.quote: Non-qualified Deferred Compensation Plan. The Partnership has a non-qualified deferred compensation plan for certain financial advisors. The Partnership has recorded a liability of $303 for the future payments due to financial advisors participating in the plan.

items.text: Edward Jones discloses that eligible retiring financial advisors are offered individually tailored retirement transition plans that compensate a retiring financial advisor for providing client transition services, generally under a five-year agreement with most paid ratably over four years.
items.quote: Retirement Transition Plans. Eligible retiring financial advisors are offered individually tailored retirement transition plans. Each retirement transition plan compensates a retiring financial advisor for successfully providing client transition services in accordance with a retirement and transition agreement.

cells.reason: The passages state several components of the financial advisor compensation structure (commission basis with minimum guaranteed salary, Program Fee portion, bonus eligibility, profits interest, travel awards, deferred compensation, and retirement transition plans), each a fact about the structure.
